<mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#ifndef M_PI\n#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT_2\n#define M_SQRT_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT1_2\n#define M_SQRT1_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n\n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n\n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n\n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n\n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n\n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Option i of the batch: a pure function of i, so any rank can build any option\ninline OptionInput makeOption(const size_t i) noexcept {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n\n    // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n    OptionInput option = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n\n    // Add some variation for larger datasets\n    const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n    option.spot *= M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9413, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9210, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Generate a larger set of options by scaling the test set\nvoid generateOptions(std::vector<OptionInput>& options, const size_t parameters slightly\n        const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n        options[i] = base;\n        \n        // Add some variation for larger datasets\n        const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n        options[i].spot *= factor;\n        options[i].strike *= factor;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const std::vector<OptionInput>& options, \n                     const std::vector<double>& results) {\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const int numChecks = std::min(static_cast<size_t>(10), options[i].value;\n        const double error = fabs(computed - expected);\n        const double relError = error / (fabs(expected) + 1e-10);\n        \n        printf(\"  Option %d: computed=%.4f, expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %d: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfzi7TGLTdAkdRvBWX9Zy","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now runs under MPI unconditionally. Its output matches the original binary, and pricing scales close to linearly with rank count.\n\n**Changes** (only `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt`; executable name still `black_scholes`):\n\n- **Partitioning:** the `N` options are split into contiguous, near-equal blocks, one per rank. Each rank builds only its own options via a new `makeOption(i)` function, which replaces `generateOptions`. No rank holds the full options array any more.\n- **Results:** rank 0 writes its block directly into the full result array. The other ranks' blocks come back through `MPI_Gatherv` with `MPI_IN_PLACE` on the root. The Kahan sum, FNV hash, min/max, sample indices and validation all still run on the full array in the original order, so their results are unchanged.\n- **Timing:** a barrier, then `MPI_Wtime` around the pricing loop only. The reported time is the maximum across ranks, so it reflects the slowest rank. The gather is excluded, as the original excluded its own post-processing.\n- **Output and exit codes:** only rank 0 prints. Every rank parses arguments identically, and the validation result is broadcast so all ranks exit with the same code.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(MPI REQUIRED)` and link `MPI::MPI_CXX`. Compile flags are unchanged.\n\n**Choices you may want to review:**\n- Pure MPI, no OpenMP, to avoid adding a hybrid dimension.\n- `N` is capped at `INT_MAX` (about 2.1 billion). MPI counts and displacements are `int`. The program prints an error and exits if `N` is larger. Lifting this would need `MPI_Gatherv_c` or chunked gathers.\n- Rank 0 still holds the full result array, because the output semantics require it.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Built with CMake (no warnings) in `/tmp`, so nothing was added to the project.\n- Compared against a pristine build of the original: 9 sizes (0 to 100,000) × 6 rank counts (1 to 8), with `-v -r`. Every output line matched except the two timing lines, and all exit codes matched.\n- The `-h`, unknown-option and over-limit error paths behave as expected.\n- Timing on 20M options (`-n 20000000`): 2.71 s on 1 rank, 1.37 s on 2, 0.68 s on 4, 0.33 s on 8. That's about 7.4M options/s on one rank and about 60M options/s on eight. The machine has 256 cores, but I only ran up to 8 ranks.\n\nThe comparison used `--oversubscribe` because of the MPI setup on this machine. I have not tested on a real multi-node cluster."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":649,"cache_read_input_tokens":40950,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":649},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c2662ad3-daf4-41ef-9b62-2a3ba4480f1e","uuid":"0ec9ef5e-75b7-4110-a0b4-5f1cedca4319","timestamp":"2026-10-13T18:28:28.978Z","request_id":"req_011Cfzi7SxEn1NmZw5GCFVvu"}
